etymologies.etymologyHTML: Borrowed from Late Latin implēmentum (“a filling up”), from Latin impleō (“I fill up”).

definitions.definition: To bring about; to put into practice; to carry out.

quote.citation: 1960 December, “The Irish Scene”, in Trains Illustrated, page 715:
quote.text: A considerable amount of beet comes from the Clonakilty and Courtmacsherry growing areas to Mallow and if the closure proposals mentioned are implemented this traffic will in future years be thrown on roads ill-suited to such heavy haulage.

quote.citation: 2021 May 29, David Hytner, “Chelsea win Champions League after Kai Havertz stuns Manchester City”, in The Guardian‎[1]:
quote.text: Guardiola, who last won the Champions League in 2011, started with no defensive midfielder and no recognised striker and watched his midfielder-heavy lineup struggle to implement a complicated gameplan.

definitions.definition: (programming) To realize a technical specification, e.g. of an algorithm, interface, or protocol.
A tool or instrument for working with.

quote.citation: 1900, Sigmund Freud, translated by James Strachey, The Interpretation of Dreams: Avon Books, page 234:
quote.text: A man dreamt as follows: He saw two boys struggling—barrel-maker’s boys, to judge by the implements lying around.
